text.S1: Once there was a miller who was poor, but who had a beautiful daughter. Now it happened that he had to go and speak to the King, and in order to make himself appear important he said to him, "I have a daughter who can spin straw into gold." The King said to the miller, "That is an art which pleases me well; if your daughter is as clever as you say, bring her to-morrow to my palace, and I will try what she can do."

text.T1: Nako yeñwi nekuna ni musiti wa mubotana yanaana ni mwana yomunde wa musizana. Cwale kwaezahala kuli naana ni kuyo ambola ni mulena ka mulelo wa kuyo iponahaza kuli ni yena ki mutu wabutokwa mi ali ku mulena, “Nina ni mwana wa musizana yaziba kufetula bucwañi bobuomile kubueza gauda.” Mulena ali ku musiti, “Boo ki bukwala bobuni tabisa hande. Haiba nji mwanaahao ubutali kuya kamoo ubulelela, mutise kwa muleneñi kamuso mi nika lika kubona sewo akona kueza.”

text.S1: And when the girl was brought to him he took her into a room which was quite full of straw, gave her a spinning-wheel and a reel, and said, "Now set to work, and if by to-morrow morning early you have not spun this straw into gold during the night, you must die." Thereupon he himself locked up the room, and left her in it alone. So there sat the poor miller's daughter, and for the life of her could not tell what to do; she had no idea how straw could be spun into gold, and she grew more and more miserable, until at last she began to weep.

text.T1: Habusa musizana hase aisizwe, mulena amuisa mwa muzuzu wone utezi bucwañi bobuomile ni kumufa liwili lelipotoloha ni sipi yetateza ni kupyata-pyata bucwañi mi ali kuyena, “Cwale itukiseze kusebeza. Haiba lufita kamuso kakusasana-sasana usika pyata bucwañi bobuomile bo kubufetula gauda mwahala busihu, ulukela kushwa.” Honafoo kasamulaho, yena mulena kasibili akiyela musizana mwa muzuzu woo ni kumusiya anoosi. Cwale mwanaa musiti wa mubotana aina fafasi! Ali kupepwa asaezi nto yecwalo mi kahoo naa sazibi sakueza. Naa sina muhupulo wa moo bucwañi bobuomile bukona kufetulwa gauda. Aikutwa hahulu bumai mane mafelelezo akala feela kulila.

text.S1: But all at once the door opened, and in came a little man, and said, "Good evening, Mistress Miller; why are you crying so?" "Alas!" answered the girl, "I have to spin straw into gold, and I do not know how to do it." "What will you give me," said the manikin, "if I do it for you?" "My necklace," said the girl. The little man took the necklace, seated himself in front of the wheel, and "whirr, whirr, whirr," three turns, and the reel was full; then he put another on, and whirr, whirr, whirr, three times round, and the second was full too. And so it went on until the morning, when all the straw was spun, and all the reels were full of gold.

text.T1: Kono ka nako yekuswani feela munyako wakwahuluha ni kukena kaana-nyana mi kali, “Ki manzibuana, muzamayisi wa basiti.Ulila sikamañi?” “Mawe!” kwaalaba musizana. Aekeza kubulela ali, “Nilukela kufetula bucwañi bobuomile kubueza gauda kono hanizibi mwa kuezeza.” “Ukanifa sikamañi?” kwabuza kaana-nyana kawo, “Haiba niku ezeza musebezi wo?” “Sifaha saaka sa mwa mulala,” kwaalaba musizana. Kaana-nyana kawo kaanga sifaha sa mwa mulala ni kuina fapilaa liwili lelipotoloha ni sipi yetateza kupyata-pyata bucwañi. Apotolosa liwili halaalu mi kwautwahala mulumo oli, “Wii! Wii! Wii!” Sipi yetateza ni kupyata-pyata bucwañi yatala Hape alonga bucwañi ni kupotolosa liwili halaaalu mi kwautwahala mulumo oli, “Wii! Wii! Wii!” Sibeyelo sabubeli hape satala. Musebezi wazwelapili cwalo kufitela kakusasana-sasana foo mabeelo kaufela atala a gauda.

text.S1: By daybreak the King was already there, and when he saw the gold he was astonished and delighted, but his heart became only greedier. He had the miller's daughter taken into another room full of straw, which was much larger, and commanded her to spin that also in one night if she valued her life. The girl knew not how to help herself, and was crying, when the door again opened, and the little man appeared, and said, "What will you give me if I spin that straw into gold for you?" "The ring on my finger," answered the girl.

text.T1: Ka nako yeli pazula lizazi mulena nasaa fitile kale kwa muzuzu koo. Cwale haa bona gauda amakala ni kutaba hahulu. Kono mwa pilu akenelwa ki muhupulo wa lunya. Hape aisa mwanaa mubeti wa musizana yoo mwa muzuzu womuñwi hape wone utezi bucwañi bobuomile, boo neli bobuñata luli kufita bwapili. Alaelwa kuli afetule ni bo kaufela mwahalaa busihu bulibuñwi haiba nji naa lata bupilo bwahae. Musizana naasa zibi sewo naaka kona kueza kuli aipuluse. Naa lila, ka nako yewo munyako hau kwahuluha hape mi kwakena kaana-nyana kale ni kubuza cwana, “Ukanifa sikamañi hanika kufetulela bucwañi bo kubueza gauda?” Lisale lelili kwa munwana waaka,” kwaalaba musizana.

text.S1: The little man took the ring, again began to turn the wheel, and by morning had spun all the straw into glittering gold.

text.S1: The King rejoiced beyond measure at the sight, but still he had not well enough; and he had the miller's daughter taken into a still larger room full of straw, and said, "You must spin this, too, in the course of this night; but if you succeed, you shall be my wife." "Even if she be a miller's daughter," thought he, "I could not find a richer wife in the whole world."

text.T1: Mulena ataba hahulu ni kufita, haato bona cwalo. Kono nihakulicwalo, naa sika kololokwa. Hape aisa mwanaa mubeti wa musizana yoo mwa muzuzu womuñwi womutuna wone utezi bucwañi bobuomile mi ali, “Ulukela kufetula bucwañi bo hape, mwahalaa busihu bwakacenu; mi haiba ufeza hande ukaba musalaka.” Aipulelela mwa pilu ali, “Nihakaaba mwanaa musiti. Nipalezwi kufumana musali wa mbombo mwa lifasi lote.”

text.S1: When the girl was alone the manikin came again for the third time, and said, "What will you give me if I spin the straw for you this time also?" "I have nothing left that I could give," answered the girl. "Then promise me, if you should become Queen, your first child." "Who knows whether that will ever happen?" thought the miller's daughter; and, not knowing how else to help herself in this strait, she promised the manikin what he wanted, and for that he once more span the straw into gold.

text.T1: Hase asiyezi anoosi mwa muzuzu moo, kaana-nyana kataha hape lwabulaalu mi kamubuza kali, “Ukanifa sikamañi hanika kufetulela bucwañi bobuomile bo hape?” "Hanisana seni siyezi ni sona seni kona kukufa,” kwaalaba musizana. "Kanti uni sepise kunifa mweeli wahao haiba nji uba Muoli,” kaana-nyana kabulela. “Ki mañi yaziba kuli nto yecwalo yakona kuezahala?” mwanaa mubeti anahana mwa pilu, kono inge asina mukwa wa omuñwi woo naaka itukululela kawona mwa kakwaci ka, kacwalo, musizana asepisa kaana-nyana ka sewo neka tabela kufiwa. Ekalaza. Hase balumelelani cwalo, kaana-nyana cwale kazwelapili mwa musebezi wa kufetula bucwañi bobuomile kubueza gauda.
